column1: # mapping_set_title: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 to NIST AI RMF Common Schema Mappings

# mapping_set_description: Schema-level mappings between the ISO/IEC 22989:2022 (Artificial intelligence concepts and terminology) and the NIST AI RMF common LinkML schema. The NIST AI RMF TrustworthinessCharacteristicEnum aligns closely with the ISO/IEC 22989 TrustworthinessPropertyType enum; rows below capture the seven characteristic-to-property correspondences plus the shared NamedThing/NamedEntity identity base.

column10: Shared identity / labelled-entity abstraction used as the root of both schemas.
ISO/IEC 22989 models trustworthiness as a first-class claim class; NIST AI RMF treats trustworthiness characteristics as an enumeration. Mapping is class-to-scheme.
Two enumerations cover the same conceptual space of trustworthiness characteristics, with different granularities.
NIST bundles validity and reliability; ISO/IEC 22989 separates them.
Both refer to absence of unacceptable risk of harm.
NIST bundles security with resilience; ISO/IEC 22989 separates the two properties.
NIST bundles resilience with security; ISO/IEC 22989 separates the two properties.
Both refer to respecting personal data and individual privacy expectations.
NIST combines fairness with bias management; ISO/IEC 22989 also has a separate bias_mitigation property.
NIST treats harmful-bias management as part of fairness; ISO/IEC 22989 models it as a distinct property.
